subject: biology

hotspots.label: Stoma pore
hotspots.description: A tiny pore on the leaf surface that opens and closes to let gases pass.
hotspots.positionHint: A small bean-shaped opening between the two guard cells.
hotspots.function: Lets carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.

hotspots.label: Guard cells
hotspots.description: The two curved cells around the pore that swell to open it and relax to close it.
hotspots.positionHint: The two crescent-shaped cells that frame the stoma opening.
hotspots.function: Open and close the pore like gates.

hotspots.label: Gas flow
hotspots.description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) enters the pore and oxygen (O2) leaves during photosynthesis.
hotspots.positionHint: Small directional dots entering and leaving the pore when the gas layer is on.
hotspots.function: Moves carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.

hotspots.label: Leaf surface
hotspots.description: The smooth outer layer of the leaf where many stomata are found.
hotspots.positionHint: The flat textured surface the stoma sits on.
hotspots.function: Holds the stomata and connects them to the leaf body.

visualStyleNotes: Anatomy Atelier bar throughout: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A clean stylized leaf-surface diorama - muted green surface, cream tones, not cartoon, not cluttered, no glow. Strong color reserved for the hotspot dots and tiny gas dots.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0, matte roughness ~0.5-0.65. No emissive.
assetBrief: SUBJECT: an enlarged view of a leaf surface showing several stomata, with one stoma magnified at center, framed by two crescent guard cells. An open/close slider toggles the guard cells bent-apart or together. Tiny colored gas dots enter (carbon dioxide) and leave (oxygen). Named nodes: LeafSurface, StomaOpen, StomaClosed, GuardCells, GasIn, GasOut. Budget 10-14k.
